hypothesis: Removing the requirement that the fresh five-minute breakout side agree with the hourly structural side may increase HYPE trade frequency without degrading after-cost outcomes.
decision: Reject removing the breakout-side alignment requirement from the live v52 route. One exact current-run long-side evaluation passed every other configured entry prerequisite but had an opposed short breakout. Its completed-candle long counterfactual was negative after the fixed thirteen-basis-point diagnostic hurdle at five, fifteen, and sixty minutes and positive only at thirty minutes. This is one readiness path rather than a fill or an exact eight-to-twenty-four-hour lifecycle, so it neither proves the alignment rule profitable nor supports relaxing it. Keep the current route unchanged and collect a predeclared independent exact-one-blocker sample.
falsifier: Reopen only after at least 20 independent exact one-blocker episodes include both structural sides and remain positive after executable costs and largest-winner removal under predeclared horizons, followed by a causal exact-route replay with the 80-basis-point stop and soft-eight-to-hard-twenty-four-hour exit contract.
limitations: One path has extreme sampling uncertainty and cannot estimate win rate, profit factor, or trade frequency.
The path is a completed-candle counterfactual, not an order, fill, fee, funding, slippage, or PnL observation.
The five-, fifteen-, thirty-, and sixty-minute horizons overlap and are not independent.
The fixed thirteen-basis-point hurdle is not realized counterfactual execution cost.
The measured horizons do not reproduce the live soft-eight-to-hard-twenty-four-hour exit contract.
Older broad direction-alignment evidence used a different route identity and contained contradictory post-hoc opposed-side results.
This revision grants no gating, sizing, routing, entry, exit, pause, retuning, or promotion authority.
